extracted.intended_audience: Tower proponents and AM station licensees; FCC applicants/petitioners with reportable foreign ownership; advanced communications service providers seeking Reimbursement Program funds
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements in 47 CFR Part 1 covering (a) notification and measurement rules for tower construction/modification near AM stations, (b) Commission referral and executive-branch review procedures for filings with reportable foreign ownership, and (c) the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program (Covered List, eligibility, filing, prioritization, disbursement, and disposal rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moment-method base impedance measurement and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tower is modified, a base impedance measurement on the modified tower shall be made as described in §73.151(c)(1) and retained in the station's records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new measured base resistance and reactance differ by more than ±2 ohms and ±4 percent respectively from the modeled values in the last moment method proof, the station must file Form 302‑AM accompanied by the new impedance measurements and a new moment method model for each pattern in which the tower radiates. Base impedance measurements for other towers in the array, sampling system measurements, and reference field strength measurements need not be repeated if the affected tower continues to meet moment method proofing requirements after modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 302‑AM filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When required to file Form 302‑AM following an installation, the Form 302‑AM shall be filed before or simultaneously with any license application associated with the installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no license application is filed as a result of the installation, the Form 302‑AM must be filed within 30 days after completion of the installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum notice period for tower construction/modification near AM stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proponents subject to §§1.30002 and 1.30003 must provide notice of proposed tower construction or significant modification to any nearby AM station at least 30 days prior to commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be provided using official licensee information and address in CDBS (or successor database). Notification may be oral or written; if oral, written documentation of the communication and date must be supplied upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum contents of tower-notification to AM stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification must include relevant technical details; at a minimum it should include the proponent's name and address and coordinates of the tower, a physical description of the planned structure, and results of any analysis showing the predicted effect on the AM pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the predictive analysis is recommended 'if performed.' The notification must contain sufficient technical details for the AM station to assess potential pattern disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: AM station response timing and content to tower notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to notification should be made as quickly as possible; any response indicating potential disturbance must specify technical details and be provided within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no response is received within 30 days, the proponent may proceed with the proposed construction or modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of 30‑day receipt date for mailed notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If notification is by mail, the date of receipt by the AM station may be ascertained by certified mail return receipt, enclosure of a dated-return card, or a conservative mailed-date estimate stated in the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a conservative estimate is used, the estimated date when the 30‑day period would expire must be stated in the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited notification requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A proponent may request an expedited notification period of less than 30 days by identifying the notification as 'expedited' and clearly indicating the requested response date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proponent may proceed prior to expiration of the 30‑day period only upon receipt of written concurrence from the affected AM station (oral concurrence allowed if followed by written confirmation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency temporary tower exception and remedy obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: In emergencies involving essential public services, a proponent may erect a temporary new tower or temporarily modify a tower without prior notice, provided written notice is given within five days and the proponent cooperates to promptly remedy any pattern distortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception is limited to immediate and urgent communications needs involving public health, welfare, or essential services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission referral discretion for filings with reportable foreign ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may refer applications, petitions, and other filings to the executive branch for review for national security, law enforcement, foreign policy, and/or trade policy concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will generally refer international section 214 authorizations, submarine cable landing licenses, assignment/transfer/modify applications with reportable foreign ownership, and certain 310(b) petitions; however, referrals are discretionary and exclusions apply (see exclusion criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from automatic referral to executive branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain filings may be excluded from referral where applicant shows one or more of: pro forma status; reportable foreign ownership only through wholly owned intermediate holding companies with ultimate U.S. ownership; existing conditioned authorization with no new foreign owners and agreement compliance; or prior executive-branch review within 18 months with no new reportable foreign owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When excluded, applicants must make a specific showing in their application demonstrating the applicable exclusion(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow referral procedures when notified
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission refers a filing to the executive branch, the applicant/petitioner/filer will be instructed to follow the requirements in this subpart, including submitting responses to standard questions to the Committee and making appropriate certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral instructions include submission processes and timelines described elsewhere in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission consideration of executive branch recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will consider recommendations from the executive branch on referred matters as part of its public interest analysis and will make an independent decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive branch input is evaluated but is not dispositive; the Commission retains ultimate authority over the public interest determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to executive branch of confidential submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may disclose to relevant executive branch agencies any information submitted in confidence pursuant to §0.457 or §0.459 when making a referral or considering recommendations, subject to 44 U.S.C. 3510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice will be provided at the time of disclosure, notwithstanding §0.442.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'reportable foreign ownership' in referral context
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Reportable foreign ownership' means (for §1.767 and §63.18/§63.24 filings) any foreign owner that must be disclosed under §63.18(h); for petitions under §§1.5000–1.5004 it means foreign disclosable interest holders per §1.5001(e) and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition ties referral triggers to specific disclosure rules in other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and deferral request procedure for executive branch review
rubrics_metrics.description: To seek executive branch review, the Commission places the referred filing on an accepted-for-filing public notice providing a comment period for the executive branch to seek deferral for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The executive branch must electronically file deferral requests in all applicable Commission file numbers/dockets and indicate tailored-questions status (sent, will send within 30 days, or will not transmit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of no executive-branch deferral request within comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the executive branch does not notify the Commission that it seeks deferral within the comment period, the Commission will deem that the executive branch has no relevant concerns and may act on the filing based on public interest determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of deferral request allows the Commission to proceed without waiting for executive-branch review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of information to provide to the executive branch when referred
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/petitioners/filers must submit detailed information on: (i) corporate structure and shareholders; (ii) relationships with foreign entities; (iii) financial condition; (iv) compliance with laws; and (v) business and operational information including services and network infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These responses to the standard questions must be submitted directly to the Committee and a complete unredacted copy of the FCC filing must be submitted to the Committee within three business days of filing with the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and submission of standard questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard questions and instructions for submitting responses and FCC filings are available on the FCC website; responses must be submitted directly to the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the FCC website for the current standard questions and follow submission instructions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored questions and completeness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive branch may send tailored questions to applicants; the Committee Chair will determine when responses are complete, which affects review timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chair's completeness determination starts the review-period timelines described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial executive-branch review timeframe (120 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive branch shall notify the Commission of its status no later than 120 days (plus additional days for escalated review and NTIA notification) from the date the Committee Chair determines an applicant's responses are complete, provided tailored questions were sent within 30 days of referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within this period the executive branch may (1) have no recommendation/object, (2) recommend grant contingent on mitigation measures, or (3) need additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary assessment timeframe (additional 90 days; total up to 210 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional time is needed beyond the initial 120 days for a secondary assessment, the executive branch must explain why and notify the Commission; the review must conclude no later than 210 days (plus escalated-review/NTIA notification days) from Chair-completeness date, subject to exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible outcomes after secondary assessment include no recommendation, conditional grant with mitigation, or recommendation to deny due to national security/law enforcement risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive-branch public notifications and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive branch must file status notifications in the public record for all applicable Commission file numbers/dockets including dates tailored questions were sent and when responses were deemed complete, and must file extension notices and updates every 30 days during a 90‑day extension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If recommending dismissal for failure to respond, the executive branch must file that recommendation in the public record. Non‑public information must be accompanied by a public version and the non‑public filing pursuant to §0.457.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative start-date and extension mechanics for review clock
rubrics_metrics.description: If the executive branch does not transmit tailored questions within 30 days of referral, it may request additional time; the Commission may allow an extension or start the 120‑day clock immediately; if no tailored questions are necessary the 120‑day period begins on the notification date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mechanisms determine the effective start of the 120‑day initial review clock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive-branch ability to extend review periods
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Executive Order 13913, the executive branch may extend the initial 120‑day and/or 90‑day secondary assessment review periods and must file notifications of all extensions in the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary and must be publicly notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered List publication and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (PSHSB) shall publish the Covered List of communications equipment and services on the Commission's website and maintain/update it per §1.50003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Covered List is regularly updated and posted publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for Covered List
rubrics_metrics.description: PSHSB shall place on the Covered List any communications equipment or service that, based exclusively on specific determinations by designated national-security sources (executive-branch interagency bodies with expertise, Department of Commerce determinations under EO 13873, section 889 definitions, or determinations by appropriate national security agencies), poses an unacceptable risk to national security or U.S. persons' safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to being based on such determinations, the equipment/service must be capable of (i) routing/redirecting user data or permitting visibility into user data/packets, (ii) causing remote disruption of provider networks, or (iii) otherwise posing an unacceptable national security/safety risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and update rules for the Covered List
rubrics_metrics.description: PSHSB will monitor determinations to update the Covered List; if a determination is reversed or modified, PSHSB shall remove or modify the entry unless another source still supports inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Covered List is not updated during a 12‑month period, PSHSB will issue a Public Notice indicating no updates were necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement Program eligibility (provider size and definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers of advanced communications service with ten million or fewer customers are eligible to participate in the Reimbursement Program for costs reasonably incurred for permanent replacement, removal, and disposal of covered communications equipment or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to definitions adopted in the Report and Order and Designation Orders; providers must meet certification requirements described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider certification requirements for Reimbursement Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The provider must certify that, as of application submission, it has developed: (A) a plan for permanent removal/replacement/disposal of covered equipment/services in its network and (B) a specific timeline for that work, which is submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning on approval date, the provider must not purchase/rent/lease/obtain covered equipment using reimbursement funds or any other funds, and must consult/consider NIST cybersecurity framework standards in tailoring risk-management practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-window procedures and simultaneous‑receipt treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Wireline Competition Bureau (WCB) will announce initial and additional application filing windows and the amount of funding available; all eligible providers filing within a window are treated as if applications were simultaneously received; funding requests submitted outside a filing window will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WCB may implement additional filing windows as necessary and will provide notice before opening them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of funding requests/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must include: (i) an estimate of costs reasonably incurred (may rely on Catalog of Expenses or submit own with supporting documentation and a good‑faith certification), (ii) detailed information on covered equipment/services being removed, (iii) required certifications, (iv) a specific timeline for removal/replacement/disposal, and (v) good‑faith certifications regarding incurring costs, use of funds, compliance with policies, record retention, and filing required documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers relying on their own cost estimates must provide supporting documentation and certify the estimate is in good faith. Records of eligible costs must be maintained for 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review timeline and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: WCB will review applications for completeness, eligibility, and reasonableness of cost estimates and shall approve or deny applications within 90 days after the close of the filing window; WCB may extend the deadline up to an additional 45 days if excessive filings require more review time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions apply when WCB determines the volume of applications warrants more time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cure period for materially deficient applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is materially deficient (including inadequate cost estimate/supporting materials), WCB shall provide a 15‑day cure period before denying the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the cure period would extend beyond the approval/denial deadline, the deadline is extended through the end of the cure period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of denial on future applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial of an application does not preclude the applicant from submitting a new application for reimbursement in a subsequent filing window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may reapply in later windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding allocation mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an application is approved, WCB will allocate funding on the applicant's behalf to the U.S. Treasury for drawdown by the Reimbursement Program recipient as expenses are incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation precedes drawdown claims; the disbursement process follows procedures in paragraph (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization schedule for allocating funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If total demand exceeds available funds, WCB will allocate funds according to priorities: Priority 1 — providers with 2 million or fewer customers; Priority 2 — accredited non‑commercial educational institutions providing facilities‑based educational broadband, health care providers, and libraries; Priority 3 — remaining approved applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WCB issues full funding allocations for all eligible providers in a priority category before moving to the next. If insufficient funds exist within a category, funds are pro‑rated among providers in that category; later categories are denied for lack of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro‑rata reduction calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When pro‑rata reductions are required, WCB will (i) divide total remaining funds by demand in the category to produce a pro‑rata factor, (ii) multiply that factor by each recipient's requested amount, and (iii) allocate funds consistent with that calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formula WCB uses to compute each recipient's allocation when funds are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement claim requirements and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Following allocation, a recipient may file reimbursement claims to draw down funds; each claim must show actual expenses reasonably incurred for removal, replacement, and disposal of covered equipment/services. WCB will review and grant or deny reimbursement claims for actual costs reasonably incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must document actual expenses and meet eligibility/certification conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial reimbursement claim deadline and consequence of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year of approval, a recipient must file at least one reimbursement claim; failure to file within one year will result in reclamation of all allocated funding from the recipient and reversion to the program fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely initial claims are required to retain allocated funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement-claim final deadline and single extension
rubrics_metrics.description: All reimbursement claims must be filed within 120 days of expiration of the removal/replacement/disposal term. A recipient may request a single extension of up to 120 days, filed no later than the original deadline; WCB shall grant any timely filed extension request for no more than 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the reimbursement claim deadline (including any granted extension), remaining unclaimed allocated funds will be reclaimed and revert to the program fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal/replacement/disposal term duration and completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must complete permanent removal, replacement, and disposal of covered equipment/services within one year of receiving the initial drawdown disbursement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one‑year term is the baseline; extensions are available under limited circumstances described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: General extension of removal term for all recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may extend the removal/replacement/disposal term by six months for all recipients if it finds that the supply of replacement equipment/services is inadequate and provides notice and detailed justification to specified congressional committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a program‑wide extension that requires findings and notice to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual extensions for recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to expiration of the term, a recipient may petition WCB for an extension of up to six months if, through no fault of the recipient, it cannot complete removal/replacement/disposal by term end; WCB may grant more than one extension if circumstances warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual extensions are granted based on recipient-specific inability to complete work, not for recipient fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of reimbursement funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not use reimbursement funds to remove/replace/dispose of any covered equipment/service purchased, rented, leased, or otherwise obtained on or after publication of the Report and Order (or June 30, 2020 for equipment newly covered per Designation Orders). Recipients also may not purchase/rent/lease/obtain covered equipment or services using reimbursement funds or any other funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is only for eligible costs reasonably incurred to remove/replace/dispose of covered equipment obtained prior to the cutoff dates; recipients must certify compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal requirements to prevent reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must dispose of covered equipment/services in a manner that prevents use in other providers' networks; disposal must destroy the equipment/services and render them permanently inoperable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposal obligations are strict: permanent inoperability is required to prevent redeployment of covered equipment.
